title: Screen-Time Fairness Across Kids
dataSources: Baby feeds (`baby:feed`), baby sleep (`baby:sleep`), diaper changes (`diaper:change`), chore completions (`chore:completion`), allowance ledger (`allowance:ledger`), family calendar (`family:calendar`), growth measurements (`growth:measurement`).
app: Baby-tracking apps (Huckleberry/Baby Daybook exports), chore and allowance boards, shared family calendars, and growth logs — sent to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=screentime:usage
| search person=*
| bin _time span=1w
| stats sum(minutes) as minutes by person _time
| stats avg(minutes) as avg_weekly by person
| eval hours=round(avg_weekly/60,1)
| sort - hours
description: Compares each child's weekly screen time so the family screen-time rules are applied evenly and arguments are settled with facts.
value: Perceived unfairness drives sibling screen-time battles; an even comparison turns a shouting match into a calm agreement.
implementation: Ingest per-child screen-time into `index=personal`; schedule weekly and compare hours across kids.
visualization: Bar chart of average weekly screen hours by child.
grandmaExplanation: It compares how much screen time each child gets, so the rules feel fair and there are fewer arguments.
